title: Bitcoin-Powered Escrow
subtitle: Our Bitcoin escrow system protects both taskers and taskees throughout the entire task process.
guideTitle: Peace of Mind Payments: A Simple Guide to Escrow
guideIntro: Think of our escrow as a smart, digital safe deposit box that holds the payment for a task until everyone agrees the job is done. It's designed to be fair, automatic, and secure, all powered by Bitcoin technology.
step1Text1: When a Tasker hires a Taskee, they place the payment into the shared digital lockbox (escrow). From this moment on, the funds are safe and can only be moved when specific conditions are met. Neither the Tasker nor the Taskee can access the funds alone, but can access them at any point, provided they both agree on the outcome.
step1Text2: The escrow period is set to 14 days after the estimated task completion date, with the option to extend it if needed. At this point, if the Taskee has not marked the task as complete, the funds are automatically returned to the Tasker.
step1Text3: This escrow process is achieved through the use of a 2-of-2 multisig wallet, which requires both the Tasker and the Taskee to agree on the outcome of the task. As these agreements are made directly between the Tasker and Taskee, BitTasker is unable to intervene in the process, creating a true peer-to-peer escrow process.
step2Title: Step 2: Completing the Task & Getting Paid
step2Text1: Once the Taskee finishes the work, they mark the task as complete. The Tasker then reviews the work.
step2List1: If the Tasker is happy, they approve the payment, and the funds are instantly released from the escrow to the Taskee.
step2List2: Safety Net: If the Tasker doesn't take any action within 7 days, the system automatically releases the funds to the Taskee. This protects Taskees from unresponsive, or forgetful Taskers.
whatIfIntro: Our system has built-in rules to handle common issues automatically and fairly.
whatIfList1: Cancellations: If the task is cancelled by either the Tasker or the Taskee for a valid reason, the money is returned to the Tasker. It's that simple.
whatIfList2: Changing the Job (Rescoping): If the job changes, the Taskee can initiate a "rescope." A small portion (10%) is released to the Taskee for their time, and the rest is returned to the Tasker to fund a new, updated task.
whatIfList3: Disputes: If the Tasker isn't satisfied, they can raise a dispute. The funds stay locked while both parties discuss a fair solution, like a partial refund. If they can't agree, the system follows a clear, time-based process that ultimately returns the funds to the Tasker. Depending on the dispute avenue and outcome, this takes place either 14 days, or 30 days after the dispute is raised.
techTitle: Under the Hood: A Technical Look at Our Bitcoin Escrow
techIntro: Our escrow system is built on the Liquid Network, a Bitcoin sidechain that enables fast, confidential transactions. We leverage 2-of-2 multisignature wallets, cryptographic timelocks, and pre-signed transactions to create a fully automated, non-custodial, and trustless process.
mechanismTitle: The Core Mechanism: 2-of-2 Multisig & Pre-Signed Transactions
mechanismText: Every escrow wallet requires two signatures to authorize a transaction, ensuring no single party can control the funds. At each stage, the system generates pre-signed transactions for every possible outcome (e.g., payment, refund). These transactions are held off-chain and only become valid when a corresponding timelock expires, or the other party provides the second signature.
lifecycleList1: Initial Setup: A Tasker funds a 2-of-2 multisig wallet. A pre-signed refund transaction is created with a 14-day timelock. If the Taskee is unresponsive, this ensures an automatic refund to the Tasker. The Taskee can also, at any time, agree to refund the Tasker (if either the Tasker or Taskee needs to cancel, for example).
lifecycleList2: Cancellation: If either party cancels, the platform facilitates the signing of a refund transaction, and the Tasker receives a full refund (platform fees are also refunded).
lifecycleList3: Task Completion: When the Taskee marks the task as done, funds move to a 2-of-2 “done wallet.” This new wallet has a 7-day timelock for automatic payment to the Taskee. The Tasker can co-sign the payment transaction at any time within this 7-day window and pay the Taskee immediately, or initiate a dispute.
lifecycleList4:
Dispute Process:
  • If a dispute is opened, funds move to a “dispute wallet” with a 14-day timelock set to refund the Tasker. This is the default outcome if no agreement is reached.
  • Either party can propose a split by creating and single-signing a new transaction. If the other party agrees and signs, the new outcome is executed immediately.
  • If the first proposal is rejected, funds move to a final dispute wallet with a 30-day timelock favoring the Tasker. This serves as the final, unchangeable fallback to ensure resolution.
lifecycleConclusion: This system favors the Tasker as the Tasker ultimately has more to lose. However, it also forces the Tasker to wait to get refunded, incentivizing the Tasker to choose a fair outcome to avoid waiting the full escrow period.
feesText: Platform fees are charged upon successful completion of a task (when the Tasker accepts or the 7-day timelock expires) and during dispute resolutions. Fees are fully refunded in the case of a valid cancellation.
